messages.content: Predict a human conditional allocation in an anonymous one-shot dictator game with another student. Before random pairing and assignment to A or B, every participant states what they would give if assigned A. A has 100 points and B has 0. A may give B 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50 points, retaining 100 minus the transfer. B passively receives the transfer. There is no threat of punishment in the current game. Ten points equal CNY 1. Participation pays CNY 5 and game earnings are retained. Earlier, the participant read about a separate game in which A gave B 20 of 100 points. The harmed recipient B or an unaffected third party C could send verbal feedback to A; when present, C had 50 points. A message described as randomly selected from a previous study criticized A: "You are selfish. You shouldn’t think only of yourself." The participant rated whether the critic was angry, happy or sad, then answered unrelated questions for about 10 minutes. They also estimated other students’ choices and approval before their own allocation. Earlier critic ratings are agreement scores (1 strongly disagree, 7 strongly agree), not the participant’s own mood. Earlier descriptive estimates are percentages of other students expected to give each stated number of points, not observed frequencies or the participant’s own transfer. Use only the earlier reports supplied. Predict the conditional A-role transfer. Output only one integer: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50, in points.

Before random pairing and assignment to A or B, every participant states what they would give if assigned A. A has 100 points and B has 0. A may give B 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50 points, retaining 100 minus the transfer. B passively receives the transfer. There is no threat of punishment in the current game. Ten points equal CNY 1. Participation pays CNY 5 and game earnings are retained. Earlier, the participant read about a separate game in which A gave B 20 of 100 points. The harmed recipient B or an unaffected third party C could send verbal feedback to A; when present, C had 50 points. A message described as randomly selected from a previous study criticized A: "You are selfish. You shouldn’t think only of yourself." The participant rated whether the critic was angry, happy or sad, then answered unrelated questions for about 10 minutes. They also estimated other students’ choices and approval before their own allocation. Earlier critic ratings are agreement scores (1 strongly disagree, 7 strongly agree), not the participant’s own mood. Earlier descriptive estimates are percentages of other students expected to give each stated number of points, not observed frequencies or the participant’s own transfer. Use only the earlier reports supplied. Predict the conditional A-role transfer. Output only one integer: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50, in points.
